correctness.rationale: The claim is mathematically correct. A cyclic word gives balanced vertex incidence on the triple graph. For each uniform triple aaa there are three incident nonpalindromic reversal pairs and the selected incidence is even, so at most two selected edges meet it. In the potential certificate, the adjacency-equality masks 000, 010, 110/011, 101 and 100/001 partition the nonpalindromic words; mask 010 excludes equal outer letters. Substitution gives the five claimed local inequality values (1,1,1,2,1) and counts (108,24,24,12,72). Reversal exclusion bounds the lambda contribution by 90, uniform triples bound the charge by 16, and balance cancels the potential. The explicit 106-symbol cycle attains the bound. An independent replay (`python3 /workspace/audit-evidence/replay.py 5`) checked all 256 local words and all cyclic witness windows, including wraparound, with no collision or palindrome; distinct windows force a fundamental period of 106. The scope's edge characterization should not be read as a converse for arbitrary disconnected balanced edge sets: a single Eulerian tour additionally needs connectivity on the support. Only the forward implication is used.
residual_risks: No claim of a formal proof-assistant check or classification of all optimizers.
